Public Portion 
 1. Discussion on the Ban of Kratom, and Confiscation Tactics. 
 
Minutes 
The Joint Public Safety and Health & Human Services Committees, chaired by Councilors Gerry 
Martin and Brian Santaniello, met to continue discussion of the statewide Kratom ban, with a 
focus on enforcement and confiscation. Commissioner Helen Caulton-Harris, Lieutenant Jamie 
Bruno, Attorney Danielle Downing, and other City representatives participated. The committee 
reviewed the Health Department's enforcement efforts following the statewide ban, including 
notification letters sent to approximately 500 retailers, educational visits, and the process for 
issuing cease-and-desist orders. Commissioner Caulton-Harris stated that the Board of Health 
had been directed not to confiscate Kratom products and that confiscation would require law 
enforcement involvement. 
 
 Lieutenant Bruno explained that the Police Department could assist the Health Department by 
conducting spot checks to determine whether retailers continue to offer Kratom for sale and 
could coordinate with Licensing and other City departments when violations are identified. He 
stated that confiscation requires appropriate legal authority and procedures for handling and 
preserving seized products as evidence. Lieutenant Bruno recommended continued coordination 
with the Law Department to determine available enforcement options and potential penalties. 
Commissioner Caulton-Harris identified approximately 12 stores where Kratom or synthetic 
cannabinoids had previously been observed and reported that some stores had voluntarily 
removed Kratom from their shelves. The committee discussed whether a local enforcement 
ordinance could provide additional authority or penalties, and the Law Department agreed to 
review what enforcement measures may legally be available to the City. 
 
 The committees planned to follow up in approximately two to four weeks after Police 
Department visits to identified retailers and further legal review. Attorney Downing was asked to 
determine whether the City Council could adopt an enforcement-only ordinance related to the 
Kratom ban. A motion to adjourn was made and approved by both committee chairs.  
 
The meeting adjourned at 5:21 p.m.
